purpose: Predeclared before any result (VGT-7, PR #31): 25 held-out evaluation songs drawn by a fixed seed from McGill Billboard 2.0.1 songs with no known BTC training-song overlap, for scoring Vibe Guitar auto charts against public, time-aligned chord annotations. Pool: one song per normalized (artist, title), canonical entry = lowest id; excluded in order: a title in BTC's UsPop2002 annotation list, an Isophonics or Robbie Williams artist, a song already on docs/annotation-eval-songs.json, fewer than 12 chord changes. Order: sha256("vgt7-billboard-heldout-v1:" + 4-digit id) ascending, ties by id; the ordered pool is docs/annotation-heldout-v1-pool.json. Upload search: two frozen YouTube queries per song read to 15 results; a result qualifies on a matching "<artist> - Topic" channel, or (PR #31 amendment, decided before any capture from the same search log) a verified official artist channel (owner badge BADGE_STYLE_TYPE_VERIFIED_ARTIST) of a matching artist whose upload description starts with "Provided to YouTube by", a matching cleaned title, none of the excluded words and a length within 2 s of annotationDurationSec; smallest difference, then Q1, then rank; songs without one are skipped and the walk stops at 25 (docs/annotation-heldout-v1-search-log.json, upload rule amended-v1; the topic-only selection is kept in docs/annotation-heldout-v1-selection-diff.json). Complexity rule (from the annotation, N and X ignored): complex when >= 20 distinct labels or >= 40% of chord time is not a plain major/minor triad; simple when <= 10 labels and < 20%; otherwise moderate. Primary analysis: unweighted mean of per-song majmin WCSR with a percentile bootstrap 95% interval over songs. Results never change the list: no redraw, no replacement.

billboard-2.0.1-lab.name: McGill Billboard 2.0 (2.0.1 LAB files; chords only, no beats)
billboard-2.0.1-lab.licenceQuote: we have made them available legally under a CC0 license, but we ask that users follow scholarly norms in any public-facing work based on upon these data by citing the following ISMIR paper
billboard-2.0.1-lab.attribution: John Ashley Burgoyne, Jonathan Wild, and Ichiro Fujinaga, 'An Expert Ground Truth Set for Audio Chord Recognition and Music Analysis', in Proceedings of the 12th International Society for Music Information Retrieval Conference (Miami, FL, 2011), pp. 633-38.
billboard-2.0.1-lab.btcTraining: Not listed in the BTC README. The chosen songs were also checked against the UsPop2002 annotation list BTC used (github.com/tmc323/Chord-Annotations, uspopLabels, 195 songs): no title match. Two Billboard candidates that are in that list (Michael Jackson 'Beat It', Billy Joel 'Just the Way You Are') were left out.
